# RTS 2024/1774 — article 16 : acquisition, développement et maintenance des systèmes TIC
Source : règlement délégué (UE) 2024/1774, article 16 « ICT systems acquisition, development, and maintenance ». Extraits du texte officiel anglais ; vérifier sur EUR-Lex.

Article 16(1): financial entities shall develop, document and implement a policy governing the acquisition, development, and maintenance of ICT systems. That policy shall:
(a) identify security practices and methodologies relating to the acquisition, development, and maintenance of ICT systems;
(c) specify measures to mitigate the risk of unintentional alteration or intentional manipulation of the ICT systems during development, maintenance, and deployment.
Article 16(2): financial entities shall develop, document, and implement an ICT systems' acquisition, development, and maintenance procedure for the testing and approval of all ICT systems prior to their use and after maintenance.
Article 16(3): the procedure shall contain source code reviews covering both static and dynamic testing, including security testing for internet-exposed systems and applications. Financial entities shall:
(a) identify and analyse vulnerabilities and anomalies in the source code;
(b) adopt an action plan to address those vulnerabilities and anomalies;
(c) monitor the implementation of that action plan.
Article 16(4): the procedure shall contain security testing of software packages no later than at the integration phase.
Article 16(5): the procedure shall provide that:
(a) non-production environments only store anonymised, pseudonymised, or randomised production data;
(b) financial entities are to protect the integrity and confidentiality of data in non-production environments.
Article 16(7): the procedure shall include controls to protect the integrity of source code of ICT systems that are developed in-house or by an ICT third-party service provider.
Article 16(8): proprietary software and, where feasible, the source code provided by ICT third-party service providers, as well as source code coming from open-source projects, are to be analysed and tested in accordance with paragraph 3 prior to their deployment in the production environment.


# Politique interne PDS-2 (Banque Kerlann, fictive) — développement sécurisé
Déclinaison interne de DORA 9(3), du RTS 2024/1774 articles 6, 7, 12 et 16 pour le code applicatif. Elle fixe les règles
précises que les textes réglementaires ne donnent pas.

| Règle | Exigence | Criticité | Fondement |
|---|---|---|---|
| PDS-2.1 | Aucun secret (mot de passe, clé, jeton) n'est écrit en clair dans le code source ni dans la configuration versionnée : les secrets viennent d'un coffre ou de variables d'environnement. | Critique | RTS 7(2) |
| PDS-2.2 | Tout appel réseau sortant vérifie le certificat TLS du serveur : la vérification n'est jamais désactivée (`verify=False` interdit). | Élevée | DORA 9(3)(a) ; RTS 6(2)(a) |
| PDS-2.3 | Les mots de passe sont hachés avec argon2, bcrypt, scrypt ou PBKDF2. MD5 et SHA-1 sont interdits pour tout usage de sécurité. | Élevée | RTS 6(3) et 6(4) |
| PDS-2.4 | La chaîne d'intégration continue exécute une analyse statique de sécurité (bandit, semgrep ou CodeQL) à chaque modification. | Moyenne | RTS 16(3) |
| PDS-2.5 | Les dépendances sont épinglées à une version exacte (`paquet==version`) et auditées en intégration continue (pip-audit ou équivalent). | Moyenne | RTS 16(4) et 16(8) |
| PDS-2.6 | Les données de test sont synthétiques et déclarées comme telles (champ `"synthetic": true`) ; aucun export de production n'est versionné. | Élevée | RTS 16(5)(a) |
| PDS-2.7 | Les réussites et les échecs d'authentification sont journalisés par l'application. | Moyenne | RTS 12(2)(c)(i) |

## Délais de remédiation
Critique : 30 jours · Élevée : 90 jours · Moyenne : 180 jours · Faible : 365 jours.

control.title: No hardcoded secrets in code
control.objective: Verify no password, key or token is written in clear text in versioned code.
control.test_procedure: GET tree to list files, then GET search with regex for password|passwd|secret|api[_-]?key|token|BEGIN.*PRIVATE KEY and GET file for hits to verify whether value comes from os.environ or vault client.
control.expected: Zero hardcoded secret values; all secrets referenced via os.environ or vault; no private keys versioned.
control.risk: Hardcoded secrets allow credential theft and unauthorized transfers.
control.recommendation: Remove hardcoded secrets and load them from vault or environment variables.
control.quote: Aucun secret (mot de passe, clé, jeton) n'est écrit en clair dans le code source ni dans la configuration versionnée : les secrets viennent d'un coffre ou de variables d'environnement.

before.expected: Zero hardcoded secret values; all secrets referenced via os.environ or vault; no private keys versioned.
before.detail: Found 3 hardcoded secret values in 3 files with 6 keyword matches.

inspection.comment: The screenshot shows app/auth.py lines 1-15 with only code references to password_hash and no hardcoded secret value visible.

control.title: TLS certificate verification enforced
control.objective: Verify outgoing calls never disable TLS certificate verification.
control.test_procedure: GET search for verify\s*=\s*False|ssl\._create_unverified|CERT_NONE|check_hostname\s*=\s*False then GET file for each hit in app/.
control.expected: Zero matches for verify=False or disabled TLS verification in app/ code.
control.risk: Disabled TLS verification enables man-in-the-middle interception of SEPA data.
control.recommendation: Remove verify=False and enforce default TLS certificate verification.
control.quote: Tout appel réseau sortant vérifie le certificat TLS du serveur : la vérification n'est jamais désactivée (`verify=False` interdit).

before.expected: Zero matches for verify=False or disabled TLS verification in app/ code.
before.detail: Found disabled TLS verification patterns in app/ code.

inspection.comment: Line 18 in app/payments.py shows requests.post with verify=False, confirming disabled TLS verification.

control.title: Approved password hashing only
control.objective: Verify passwords use argon2, bcrypt, scrypt or PBKDF2 and not MD5/SHA-1.
control.test_procedure: GET search for argon2|bcrypt|scrypt|pbkdf2|hashlib\.(md5|sha1)\(|Crypto\.Hash\.(MD5|SHA1) then GET file for hits to confirm password context.
control.expected: Password hashing uses only argon2/bcrypt/scrypt/PBKDF2; zero MD5/SHA-1 use for security in app/.
control.risk: Weak hashes allow password recovery and authentication bypass.
control.recommendation: Replace MD5/SHA-1 with argon2, bcrypt, scrypt or PBKDF2 for password hashing.
control.quote: Les mots de passe sont hachés avec argon2, bcrypt, scrypt ou PBKDF2. MD5 et SHA-1 sont interdits pour tout usage de sécurité.

before.expected: Password hashing uses only argon2/bcrypt/scrypt/PBKDF2; zero MD5/SHA-1 use for security in app/.
before.detail: MD5/SHA-1 password hashing found in app/auth.py while only argon2/bcrypt/scrypt/PBKDF2 is allowed.

inspection.comment: Line 8 of app/auth.py implements hash_password with hashlib.md5 for password verification.

control.title: CI static security analysis present
control.objective: Verify CI runs bandit, semgrep or CodeQL on every change.
control.test_procedure: GET tree to list .github/workflows/ files, then GET file for each workflow and check for bandit|semgrep|CodeQL and on: [push, pull_request].
control.expected: At least one workflow runs bandit or semgrep or CodeQL on push/pull_request.
control.risk: Missing static analysis leaves code vulnerabilities undetected.
control.recommendation: Add bandit, semgrep or CodeQL step to CI on every change.
control.quote: La chaîne d'intégration continue exécute une analyse statique de sécurité (bandit, semgrep ou CodeQL) à chaque modification.

before.expected: At least one workflow runs bandit or semgrep or CodeQL on push/pull_request.
before.detail: No workflow in .github/workflows/ runs bandit, semgrep or CodeQL on push and pull_request.

inspection.field_text:
on: [push]
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: actions/setup-python@v5
- run: pip install -r requirements.txt pytest
- run: pytest -q
inspection.comment: The workflow triggers only on push and runs only checkout, setup-python, pip install and pytest with no bandit, semgrep or CodeQL step.

control.title: Pinned dependencies with CI audit
control.objective: Verify exact version pinning and CI dependency audit.
control.test_procedure: GET file for requirements.txt and verify each line matches paquet==version, then GET tree and file for .github/workflows/ and search for pip-audit|safety|dependabot|osv-scanner.
control.expected: All dependencies use == exact pin; CI contains pip-audit or equivalent audit step.
control.risk: Unpinned or unaudited dependencies allow vulnerable package deployment.
control.recommendation: Pin all dependencies with == and add pip-audit step in CI.
control.quote: Les dépendances sont épinglées à une version exacte (`paquet==version`) et auditées en intégration continue (pip-audit ou équivalent).

before.expected: All dependencies use == exact pin; CI contains pip-audit or equivalent audit step.
before.detail: Found 2 unpinned dependencies out of 3 and no CI audit step found.

inspection.comment: Screenshot shows flask with no version and requests>=2.0, confirming two unpinned dependencies.

control.title: Synthetic test data only
control.objective: Verify test data is declared synthetic and no production dump is versioned.
control.test_procedure: GET tree and search for synthetic and GET file for tests/fixtures to verify "synthetic": true, and search for production dump patterns.
control.expected: Test fixtures contain "synthetic": true; zero versioned production exports or real IBAN datasets.
control.risk: Production data in test exposes confidentiality and violates anonymisation.
control.recommendation: Replace test data with synthetic data flagged synthetic true and remove production exports.
control.quote: Les données de test sont synthétiques et déclarées comme telles (champ `"synthetic": true`) ; aucun export de production n'est versionné.

before.expected: Test fixtures contain "synthetic": true; zero versioned production exports or real IBAN datasets.
before.detail: Test fixture does not declare synthetic true.

control.title: Authentication success and failure logging
control.objective: Verify application logs both successful and failed authentications.
control.test_procedure: GET search for logger|logging|log.*auth|login.*(success|fail)|401|403 in app/ then GET file for hits to confirm both success and failure paths logged.
control.expected: Code contains log statements on both authentication success and failure paths.
control.risk: Missing auth logs prevents detection of brute-force and incident response.
control.recommendation: Add logging for both authentication successes and failures.
control.quote: Les réussites et les échecs d'authentification sont journalisés par l'application.

before.expected: Code contains log statements on both authentication success and failure paths.
before.detail: app/payments.py contains no success or failure authentication log statements.

inspection.comment: app/payments.py shows only a transfer initiation log and no authentication success or failure logs.

requirements.quote: financial entities shall develop, document and implement a policy governing the acquisition, development, and maintenance of ICT systems.
requirements.summary: A documented acquisition, development and maintenance policy must exist.
requirements.why: Existence and content of a policy requires document review and is not visible in code.

requirements.quote: identify security practices and methodologies relating to the acquisition, development, and maintenance of ICT systems;
requirements.summary: The policy must identify security practices and methodologies.
requirements.why: Policy content can only be verified by reviewing the policy document.

requirements.quote: specify measures to mitigate the risk of unintentional alteration or intentional manipulation of the ICT systems during development, maintenance, and deployment.
requirements.summary: The policy must specify anti-alteration measures for development and deployment.
requirements.why: Measures description requires policy and procedure documents, not code alone.

requirements.quote: financial entities shall develop, document, and implement an ICT systems' acquisition, development, and maintenance procedure for the testing and approval of all ICT systems prior to their use and after maintenance.
requirements.summary: A testing and approval procedure before use and after maintenance must exist.
requirements.why: Testing and approval records require document review beyond read-only code access.

requirements.quote: the procedure shall contain source code reviews covering both static and dynamic testing, including security testing for internet-exposed systems and applications.
requirements.summary: Source code reviews must cover static and dynamic including security testing.
requirements.why: Static testing execution is visible in CI configuration testable via the repository interface.

requirements.quote: identify and analyse vulnerabilities and anomalies in the source code;
requirements.summary: Vulnerabilities and anomalies in source code must be identified and analysed.
requirements.why: Identification records and analysis reports require document review, not just code search.

requirements.quote: adopt an action plan to address those vulnerabilities and anomalies;
requirements.summary: An action plan to remediate vulnerabilities must be adopted.
requirements.why: An action plan is a governance document not observable in the code repository.

requirements.quote: monitor the implementation of that action plan.
requirements.summary: Implementation of the remediation action plan must be monitored.
requirements.why: Monitoring requires follow-up records and tracking, not testable via read-only code.

requirements.quote: the procedure shall contain security testing of software packages no later than at the integration phase.
requirements.summary: Software packages must undergo security testing at integration at the latest.
requirements.why: Integration-phase package auditing is visible in CI and dependency files via the repository interface.

requirements.quote: non-production environments only store anonymised, pseudonymised, or randomised production data;
requirements.summary: Non-production must only store anonymised, pseudonymised or randomised production data.
requirements.why: Versioned test data content is searchable in the repository to verify synthetic nature.

requirements.quote: financial entities are to protect the integrity and confidentiality of data in non-production environments.
requirements.summary: Integrity and confidentiality of non-production data must be protected.
requirements.why: Protection measures for environments require document and configuration review beyond code content.

requirements.quote: the procedure shall include controls to protect the integrity of source code of ICT systems that are developed in-house or by an ICT third-party service provider.
requirements.summary: Controls must protect integrity of in-house or third-party developed source code.
requirements.why: Source-code integrity controls require branch protection and signing records not exposed by file content API.

requirements.quote: proprietary software and, where feasible, the source code provided by ICT third-party service providers, as well as source code coming from open-source projects, are to be analysed and tested in accordance with paragraph 3 prior to their deployment in the production environment.
requirements.summary: Third-party and open-source code must be analysed and tested before production.
requirements.why: Dependency pinning and audit in CI visible via repository is the testable implementation of this clause.

requirements.quote: Aucun secret (mot de passe, clé, jeton) n'est écrit en clair dans le code source ni dans la configuration versionnée : les secrets viennent d'un coffre ou de variables d'environnement.
requirements.summary: No hardcoded secrets in versioned code or config; secrets come from vault or environment.
requirements.why: Hardcoded secrets patterns are searchable and verifiable via file content in the repository.
